title: ASIRT says man killed by Calgary police was wielding a metal spike
article: Alberta's police watchdog says a man shot to death by Calgary police had been wielding a one-metre-long metal spike.

Five Calgary Police Service officers were called to an abandoned building in the Franklin Industrial Park around 4:19 a.m. on Feb. 14, after a security guard found broken glass and evidence of a break-in.

According to the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, officers entered the building and heard shouting coming from a washroom. When the man inside refused officer commands to exit, two officers drew their stun guns while a third drew a firearm, and all three entered the washroom.

ASIRT said the man emerged from a stall and charged at an officer while raising the metal spike. Officers deployed their stun guns but failed to stop the man. After one officer was struck by the metal spike, another officer fired a service weapon, striking the man.
An officer who was a former medic attempted first aid on the assailant, who was declared dead at the scene by EMS.
ASIRT says the officer who was struck by the man received minor injuries.

Family members of the shooting victim have identified him as Mitch Croston, 34. His mother, Shelley Croston, told Postmedia her son was dealing with schizophrenia and drug addiction at the time of his death.

ASIRT, which investigates all incidents of police use of force in Alberta that result in serious injury or death, says its continuing investigation will determine if the force used in this case was appropriate.
The watchdog said no additional details would immediately be released.
